subject: 0620D9E3C183E6CF5D3FD17DD58C9ABC
introduction: In a religion without clergy, those who travel and teach hold the place of honour. These passages thank them, promise them the Spirit’s aid and lasting remembrance, direct that their expenses be met, and remind them that “the responsibility of the steadfast teachers is great” and that the Cause depends on “goodly deeds”. Daniel’s promise that those who “turn many to righteousness” will shine as stars, Paul’s “how beautiful are the feet”, and the sayings on the labourer’s hire are the scriptural background. James’s warning, “be not many masters”, and Jesus’s ranking of teachers by their practice give the other side of the honour.
questions: Reading 2 asks lifelong gratitude to the person who first taught one. Who has done that for you, in any field?
The readings provide for teachers’ support but have no clergy. What is the difference between a supported teacher and a professional priest?
James warns that teachers are judged more strictly. Why?

outside.why: The Pen calls without ceasing, and how few have inclined their ear. The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.
Be deeply thankful to thy teacher. Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.
Andrew is remembered for one thing: he first findeth his own brother Simon, and he brought him to Jesus.
These are the blessed souls. They that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever.

“The responsibility of the steadfast teachers is great.” James turns the greatness into a warning: my brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation. What makes teaching dangerous to the teacher?
One man who worked for God and not for fame was greater than a million divines. We preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord.
Provide the teachers a monthly sum, and more if they ask. The labourer is worthy of his hire.
Paul’s rule, which he did not use himself: they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel.
Serve whoever was the cause of your guidance. How shall they hear without a preacher? How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace.
Such teachers are lamps of guidance. Ye are the light of the world.
A high station for souls severed from the world. Every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or lands, for my name’s sake, shall receive an hundredfold.
Happy is the one who has arisen to teach. He that winneth souls is wise.
Whoever teaches, the Spirit will aid him. I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay.
No deed is greater. He which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death.
How many philosophers there are, and the crown of faith is set on thy head. Not many wise men after the flesh are called.
“Your names will go down through all the ages.” This also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.
A teacher compared to the bearer of Joseph’s garment. When the bearer of glad tidings came, he laid it on his face and he became a seer once more.
His special favour was to send a person out to teach. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations.

The triumph of the Cause depends on holy souls and goodly deeds. Jesus ranks teachers by whether they do what they teach: whosoever shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven. Why do the readings end with deeds?
Chaucer’s one good churchman is praised for the same order of things: first he wrought, and afterward he taught.

corinthians-live-of-the-gospel.text: Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel
